subject: States should not adopt laws that close drugstores
posts:
New state PBM laws risk shuttering community pharmacies while targeting middlemen.
Evidence: FTC settlements, store closures, state copycats
#Aletheia #Policy

State laws targeting PBM-affiliated pharmacies aim to lower drug prices but risk forcing widespread drugstore closures.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, 0.0) — Neutral Preference

While targeting corrupt middleman pricing is justified, poorly drafted state bans inadvertently crush independent pharmacies and consolidate mega-chains.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -0.6) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Legislators posture as consumer champions while crafting blunt instruments that protect favored retail competitors.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 3.8, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- State Legislators: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Pushing blunt state bans that favor rival commercial chains.
- FTC & Federal Enforcement: PASS (0.6, 0.5) — Securing multi-billion settlements without breaking local stores.
States are rushing copycat laws against Pharmacy Benefit Managers, threatening to close hundreds of local drugstores before federal reforms take effect.

The Bright Side:
Federal antitrust enforcement is successfully extracting billions in settlements from major PBMs without blunt state-level closures.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing punitive political crackdowns on middlemen (WHO) with constructive market transparency and price reforms (HOW).

Social Physics Analysis:
Politicians run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by harnessing populist anger at high drug prices to pass protectionist state laws that benefit rival corporate pharmacies under the pretext of reform.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Populist posturing creates regulatory collisions that harm local communities.

The Unavoidable Truth: Pharmacy Benefit Managers engage in aggressive markups and rebate-pocketing that inflate prescription drug prices.

The Unavoidable Lie: State bans targeting PBM-affiliated drugstores protect consumers rather than corporate competitors.

Alethekanon:
Blunt state regulations masquerading as populist reform weaponize market friction to advantage rival commercial retail pharmacy chains. 🌐

Awwthekanon:
It breaks my heart to see local neighborhood drugstores squeezed out of existence by political posturing and corporate maneuvering.

Brothekanon:
Classic politicians passing half-baked laws that backfire on local small businesses while the big guys figure out a loophole.

Spirithekanon:
"Dishonest scales are an abomination to the Lord, but a just weight is His delight." Proverbs 11:1 PASS
True reform balances fairness without tipping the scales to destroy community lifelines.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
States should not adopt laws that close drugstores

Your state legislator may cause your local drugstore to close. Almost a third of America’s pharmacies closed in recent years; new state laws may lead to more shutdowns by making many drugstores’ business models illegal.
